Leeds United’s hopes of signing Porto defender Zaidu Sanusi have suffered a setback, with the Portuguese club working to tie the Nigerian down to a new contract before the January transfer window. According to A Bola, Porto president André Villas-Boas wants an agreement with the left-back before the end of December. No deal is in place yet, but talks are progressing, and the club hopes to finish the renewal before the player enters the final six months of his contract, which expires at the end of the season. The 29-year-old is important to coach Francesco Farioli. Despite missing almost two months with an injury, he has played 10 of Porto’s 16 games this season, starting eight. He came off the bench against Napoli in the Champions League and lifted Porto’s attacking threat. Leeds, who are seventh in the Premier League under Daniel Farke, are said to want a January move to beat other suitors to a possible free transfer in the summer, according to Football Insider. Sanusi would add competition for Sweden international Gabriel Gudmundsson, who has started most of their league games. Should he reach January unsigned, Sanusi can negotiate a pre-contract with clubs outside Portugal. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources Aliyu Ibrahim, a confidant of the player, told Footy-Africa that Leeds have made a strong approach, while clubs from Saudi Arabia and Qatar are also interested. “Zaidu wants to remain at Porto, but it all depends on what his club can offer him in terms of a new deal. That is the situation at the moment. His first option is to stay in Portugal because he has been there for almost 10 years now. He is used to the country, the weather and the food, and he speaks fluent Portuguese too,” Ibrahim said. He added that the decision could rest with the club. “I am sure the coach likes him and wants him to stay, but everything is in the hands of the club. They have to decide whether they want to sell him to the clubs interested in signing him. There are at least three clubs looking at him.” Sanusi joined Porto from Santa Clara in 2020 and has won two Primeira Liga titles with the club.
